questions.question: What should you do when a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street?

options.text: You must always give them the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only need to give them the right-of-way at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must always give the right-of-way to anyone using a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A left turn.
An upcoming stop.
A right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A left turn.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand and arm signals instead of turn signals. A left arm held straight out means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap and shoulder belts. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. If your vehicle has an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle the lap belt.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing sign?

options.text: Drive faster than any train.
Find a way around any lowered gates.
Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing signs warn you that a train might be coming. Always obey railroad crossing signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to construction.
The road ahead makes a sharp turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead makes a sharp turn.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead. This sign tells you to slow down for a sharp change in the road direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert you to upcoming conditions. This sign warns you that a side road intersects ahead.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Closer behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have bigger blind spots. You need to follow farther behind a truck than you would a passenger vehicle.

questions.question: Who can use handicap parking spaces?

options.text: Only drivers with the correct license plate or hanging tag.
Anyone, but only when all other spaces are full.
People who are not feeling well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers with the correct license plate or hanging tag.
questions.explanation: Handicap parking spaces are for people with disabilities only. You must have the correct license plate or hanging tag to park in a handicap space.

questions.question: What happens when you drive on gravel or dirt roads?

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires have less traction on gravel and dirt than on paved roads. Slow down on gravel or dirt. It takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Driving faster than the speed limit or driving too fast for road conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving faster than the speed limit or driving too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions cause many crashes. Always drive at the legal speed limit and match the speed of traffic around you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road widens.
Right lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that the right lane is ending. Be ready for cars to merge into your lane.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may drive through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can proceed. First check that the intersection is clear of other traffic and pedestrians before driving through.

questions.question: On a two-lane road, if you drive faster and pass many cars, you will:

options.text: Reach your destination much faster and safer.
Increase your risk of a crash.
Help reduce traffic jams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Each time you pass a car, your crash risk goes up.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: They do not react as quickly as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks. They may ride bikes onto the road without warning.

questions.question: When a school bus stops with its stop arm out and red lights flashing, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think the children are done getting off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: Stop completely when you see a school bus with its stop arm extended and red lights on. Stay stopped until the arm goes up and the lights turn off.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Drive at your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down in work zones and stay alert. Follow posted speed limits. Workers may be present.

questions.question: Which is true about changing lanes?

options.text: Only look over your right shoulder for all lane changes.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Cars with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure the next lane is clear.

questions.question: If a pedestrian is crossing the street illegally instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: Always stop for pedestrians. Even if they are crossing illegally, you must still yield to them.

questions.question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Press hard on the accelerator.
Check your mirrors for traffic.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before stopping. Be aware of other drivers as you slow down. Then press the brake pedal smoothly to stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is dangerous when driving in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely
Not watching carefully for workers and equipment
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and do not follow other vehicles too closely. Watch carefully for workers and machines.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Traffic light ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. If a solid yellow line is on your side and a broken line is on the other side, you cannot pass. If both lines are solid, nobody can pass from either direction.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back into your eyes and reduce visibility.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating foods high in fat
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to process alcohol. Eating, drinking, or anything else cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass at 10 mph or slower.
Stop. Move forward only when all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop. Move forward only when all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. There may be pedestrians you cannot see. Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: Before returning to your original lane after passing, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview mirror and see both headlights of the passed vehicle before moving back into your lane.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and work zones:

options.text: Have a red background with green writing.
Have an orange background with black writing.
Have a yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that another road crosses ahead.

questions.question: It is unlawful to:

options.text: Pass in a marked no passing zone.
Pass over a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass at no passing zones, railroad crossings, street crossings, hills, curves, or when you cannot see far ahead. Do not pass when another vehicle has stopped for a pedestrian or in work zones.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic going straight. Always yield to pedestrians.
